scenarioStory.history: Patient was mowing his lawn approximately 30 minutes ago when he developed sudden-onset crushing substernal chest pain, 9/10, radiating to his left arm and jaw, associated with diaphoresis and nausea. Pain has not improved with rest. Denies similar pain before today.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: 58-year-old male found sitting in his backyard with acute-onset crushing chest pain radiating to the left arm and jaw, diaphoretic and anxious, pain 9/10. Vitals show sinus tachycardia and mild hypertension consistent with an acute cardiac event, though the 12-lead has not yet been acquired. → 12-lead acquired, STEMI Anterior recognized: 12-lead EKG acquired within the target window shows ST-segment elevation across V1-V4 consistent with an anterior STEMI. Crew activates the STEMI system of care with advance hospital notification, gives aspirin, and establishes IV access. → PDE5 use identified, NTG withheld, fentanyl given: Crew identifies the patient's sildenafil use within the past 48 hours and correctly withholds nitroglycerin due to the risk of profound, refractory hypotension. Fentanyl is administered for ongoing severe pain. → Transport to PCI center: Pain is controlled, vital signs are stable, and serial 12-lead EKGs continue to show the anterior STEMI pattern. The patient is packaged and transported to the PCI-capable receiving facility with continued monitoring and hospital updates.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: 58-year-old male found sitting in his backyard with acute-onset crushing chest pain radiating to the left arm and jaw, diaphoretic and anxious, pain 9/10. Vitals show sinus tachycardia and mild hypertension consistent with an acute cardiac event, though the 12-lead has not yet been acquired.
relatedChecklist: Perform rapid focused assessment; recognize signs/symptoms consistent with ACS
Assess cardiac rhythm; address any pulseless, symptomatic tachycardia, or symptomatic bradycardia first
Obtain complete SAMPLE history including full medication list
Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact; identify STEMI

scenarioEvents.name: 12-lead acquired, STEMI Anterior recognized
scenarioEvents.description: 12-lead EKG acquired within the target window shows ST-segment elevation across V1-V4 consistent with an anterior STEMI. Crew activates the STEMI system of care with advance hospital notification, gives aspirin, and establishes IV access.
relatedChecklist: Activate STEMI alert; transmit 12-lead and provide advance notification to receiving hospital
Aspirin 324 mg PO, chewable non-enteric-coated (within 162-325 mg range)
Establish IV access
Screen for PDE5 inhibitor use before considering nitroglycerin; withhold NTG given sildenafil 12 hours ago
Fentanyl 95 mcg IV for pain unresponsive to nitrates being contraindicated (95 kg × 1 mcg/kg = 95 mcg; max initial dose 100 mcg)

scenarioEvents.name: PDE5 use identified, NTG withheld, fentanyl given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew identifies the patient's sildenafil use within the past 48 hours and correctly withholds nitroglycerin due to the risk of profound, refractory hypotension. Fentanyl is administered for ongoing severe pain.
relatedChecklist: Reassess pain score and vital signs after analgesic administration; document response
Transport to appropriate PCI-capable facility per regional STEMI system of care

scenarioEvents.name: Transport to PCI center
scenarioEvents.description: Pain is controlled, vital signs are stable, and serial 12-lead EKGs continue to show the anterior STEMI pattern. The patient is packaged and transported to the PCI-capable receiving facility with continued monitoring and hospital updates.
relatedChecklist: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs, especially with any clinical change
Provide early notification to receiving facility of any condition changes or serial EKG findings

scenarioEvents.name: 12-lead delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew becomes distracted by scene management and does not acquire the 12-lead EKG within the 10-minute target window. STEMI recognition and hospital notification are delayed, prolonging total ischemic time.
relatedChecklist: Immediately acquire 12-lead EKG; recognize delayed diagnosis increases morbidity/mortality risk

scenarioEvents.name: NTG given without PDE5 screen
scenarioEvents.description: Nitroglycerin is given without first screening for recent PDE5 inhibitor use. Because the patient took sildenafil approximately 12 hours earlier, he develops profound, refractory hypotension requiring immediate intervention.
relatedChecklist: Recognize NTG-induced hypotension; hold further nitrates and position patient supine
IV fluid bolus to treat NTG/PDE5-induced hypotension; reassess blood pressure closely

scenarioEvents.name: STEMI progresses to VF arrest
scenarioEvents.description: Prolonged, unrecognized anterior STEMI progresses to ventricular fibrillation. The patient becomes pulseless and unresponsive, requiring immediate high-quality CPR and defibrillation.
relatedChecklist: Recognize pulselessness; begin high-quality chest compressions immediately
Defibrillate coarse VF per biphasic protocol (e.g., Zoll 120 J, 150 J, 200 J escalating)
Resume chest compressions immediately after each shock; no pause for pulse checks for 2 minutes
Establish IV/IO access; administer Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO during CPR
Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO for shock-refractory VF; may repeat 150 mg in 4-6 minutes
